subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.

requests.what: A vermilion hanko seal with a gold border on the forehead: a small square plate with an inset swirl glyph in PAPER, ink-outlined in SUMI.
Wisps of dream-smoke curling from the trunk tip: three stacked, flat-coloured curling ribbons in WAVE and PAPER with SUMI outline strokes, as printed cloud scrolls.
Richer mane along the neck crest: overlapping flame blades fading VERMILION_D to VERMILION to GOLD tips, with PAPER curl accents at the base.
A large Hokusai-style cloud scroll on each shoulder: concentric curled ribbons in GOLD and PAPER with SUMI outline, plus small trailing curls, seated on the flank.
A band of stylised seigaiha wave scallops in WAVE and PRUSSIAN with PAPER crests running along the lower flank on both sides.
Fuller lion-like tail tuft: more flame blades around the tail tip in VERMILION, GOLD and PAPER, with a gold band at the base of the tuft.
Tiger-like claws and ink-outlined toe pads for each paw, plus a vermilion fur ruff above each paw.
A gold ring earring with a vermilion tassel on each ear, and inked fur lines inside the ear in SUMI.
Kabuki-style vermilion brow sweeps and ink lash lines around each eye, extending in a flick toward the temple.
Woodblock texture on the body: INDIGO with fine darker INDIGO_DEEP grain lines, soft bokashi gradient to PRUSSIAN toward the belly, cream saddle with a PAPER_D paper-fibre speckle.
Trunk with fine PAPER ring wrinkles, a pale BLUSH tip and sumi ink hairlines.
Ears with a PAPER rim, BLUSH inner and bokashi to INDIGO_DEEP at the base.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the baku as a hybrid creature combining a tapir body, elephant trunk, tiger paws, and lion mane, designed in a flat-color ukiyo-e style with indigo and vermilion tones, curly cloud motifs, and mane flames for visual flourish.

Now I'm defining the skeleton structure: a hip root, spine chain, neck, head with jaw and trunk segments, legged limbs with IK, and a tail chain, sized to roughly tapir proportions around 2m long and 1.1m tall. I'm setting up the color palette with indigo, Prussian blue, paper cream, vermilion, sumi black, gold, and wave blue, then working out where the body's saddle markings and sweep radii go along the spine and neck joint chains.

For the head I'll use a scaled sphere part attached to the head bone for the skull ellipsoid, then sweep the trunk chain with a shrinking radius down to a nostril tip, and add tusks as spikes off the head.

Still placing facial features...

Now I'm setting up the jaw, eyes with black pupils, flattened ear shapes, and mane spikes along the neck, then starting the leg structure with hip-to-foot positions and bend directions per side.

I'm working out paw placement details so the sphere's flattened scale keeps the bottom just above the ground plane, then starting to sketch the tail chain with a curved catmull spline running back from the hips.

Next I'm defining four tail segments with decreasing sweep radii, parenting them to the hips, and planning a flame-like tuft at the tip in vermilion and gold. Then I'm sketching saddle-shaped sectors along the body sweep for shading contrast and considering spiral cloud motifs on the flank.

For the cloud swirls, I plan to stick torus arcs onto the body surface near azimuth 90, elevation 10, rotating the torus geometry so its axis aligns with the surface normal, creating concentric gold rings resembling cloud swirls.

Now I'm thinking about the mane—extruding small flame-shaped outlines along the top of the neck with alternating colors, keeping proportions simple since head and ear height tops out around 1.4. For the stuck decorative elements, I'll attach them via bones so they follow the body parts correctly.

I need named parts for texturing—body, neck, trunk, ears—and should check if sweep operations support naming. For the face, I'm planning simple ink-outline eyes with white and black pupils, plus eyebrows and nostrils, positioned relative to the skull center near the head joint.

Now I'm working out the eye placement math against the skull ellipsoid, checking whether the proposed coordinates land on or near the surface, and settling on using azimuth/elevation hit calculations to stick spheres for the eyes with slight embedding.

Then I'm placing the pupils just off the eye surface along the normal direction, and sketching ear ellipsoids with cream inner coloring. Next I'm moving into writing the actual code structure, including types and a flame-shaped mane outline.

Now for the tail, I'm fanning out spike extrusions from the tail tip, varying their direction and alternating colors between vermilion and another shade for a tufted look.

For toes, I'm adding small cream spheres at each paw tip bone to represent individual digits, then building the jaw as a box attached to a jaw joint parented under the head, aimed slightly downward and forward. I'm starting on tusk geometry next.

For the saddle, I'm shading the rear half of the body pale, spanning from hips to chest, with the hip area capped by a rounded dome. I'm checking proportions too—with the body radius and spine height, the total figure comes out close to tapir shoulder height, so I'm considering scaling it down a bit since this is meant to be a smaller spirit creature.

Now for the neck, I'm setting up a bone chain with a radius taper of roughly 0.26 down to 0.2 across four evenly spaced points, then finalizing the shape.
